hypothesis: The SunstoneOS image starts on the virtual eight-core board through startup to the first application task in the supervised and resident lifetimes, and each fault case ends as specified.

conditions.board: platform/qemu-os, virtual eight-core board; FreeRTOS SMP port with patches/
conditions.check: checks/qemu-os-boot.py builds and boots in about eight seconds
conditions.negative_control: git show 15914f7c^:apps/os/services.c passed as --services-source: the normal start then fails with failure 0x757

narrative: The image links apps/os (application, services, session, start, thermal, admission), apps/board/main.c, the thermal, clock-lease, rail-lease, PMIC, power-domain, pin and GPU-resource driver cores with their adapters, and a real application, all unmodified. Cases: Normal start (scripted sensors, USB transport ready 30 ms after its task starts): ss_live() is 1 at the application's main entry on core 2; hello-compute finishes and returns the Adler-32 of its input. Zero sealed deadline (the earlier apps/os/services.c comparing every application wait with the sealed deadline): the first wait is refused and the application stops with failure 0x757. Sensors not yet read (two sensors answer at 900 ms): the application starts with ss_throttled() 1, finishes, and the throttle clears after the last answer. Sensor lost (one never answers): after five seconds the thermal owner ends the session with a thermal failure record. Service start fault (erased calibration, closed sensor clock or a held PMIC bus line): a failure record names the thermal or PMIC owner within one second. Latency CPU control (A76 composition with latency instrumentation): the application reaches its main entry on core 6 with the OS live, then ends with failure 0xb03 because it requires the CPU clock owner's record to show the top operating points. Resident start (four-second watchdog armed by the loader): the supervisor renews the watchdog, the session runs past the first expiry and the application finishes. Resident service stall (USB transport stops reporting 100 ms after it was ready): the supervisor stops renewing and stops with status 5, naming the transport as the first stale service. Resident service silent (the transport never reports): the watchdog resets the board at its first expiry and the application never starts.

hypothesis: The remaining applications start on the virtual board.
prediction: latency with DMA needs the OS DMA service, which requires the returning lifetime and the DMA controller; queue-add, queue-gemm, gpu-fast and gpu-lifecycle need the GPU or NPU service; usb-input, usb-serial and usb-camera need the USB host, Type-C and class services; cpu-npu-load and cpu-reliability need the returning lifetime and the CPU clock owner; mimus needs the C++ runtime, the speech services and the CPU clock owner.
conclusion: Not run: the virtual board does not model those services.
narrative: Only hello-compute runs to its normal finish; the latency CPU control reaches its main entry and ends with failure 0xb03.
